You are a master of the arcane, always having the right tool for the job.

Prepared Abilities

As an Arcanist, your collection of magic spells and abilities is vast, but limited. The abilities you have selected and can use are called your Prepared Abilities. You can only have a specific number of Signature and Heroic Abilities prepared at a time, as shown on the Arcanist Advancement table, and must swap abilities out with Flash Recall or Pore Over Pages to use others.

The Arcanist uses "prepared" to refer to abilities that they can currently use. As the Arcanist levels, they will have access to multiple abilities at once, but only a certain amount of them can be "prepared" and used by the Arcanist. For example, the Arcanist has access to two triggered actions from their magical schools, but can only use one at a time. They can use Flash Recall or Pore Over Pages to swap which one they have access to, allowing for a flexible and utility-driven playstyle.

Component Prerequisites

Arcanist abilities are not only fueled by their focus, but also a physical anchor to their world in the form of Components. Seemingly mundane items required for advanced magical techniques. Unless otherwise noted, components are not consumed and can be used freely.

You know of every ability within this class that is presented at your current level, but can't prepare an ability whose Component Prerequisite you do not have. As long as you have an ability's Component Prerequisite, including if you find it while adventuring or receive it as a reward, you can prepare that ability by using Flash Recall or Pore Over Pages. When leveling up in this class, you will automatically receive the components of new abilities you choose.

Glossary: Expanded Conditions and Effects

The Arcanist uses new named conditions, effects, and terminology, some of which are borrowed from the Draw Steel Brewery Expanded Glossary.

  • Disoriented: A disoriented creature has line of effect only within 3 squares.

  • Safely: When a creature is safely force-moved, they cannot be moved in such a way that would harm them, cause them to fall, leave them dying, or otherwise result in them suffering a condition or negative effect.

  • Recurring Damage: A creature afflicted with recurring damage takes the specified type and amount of damage at the start of each of their turns.

  • Cleanse: To "cleanse an effect" on a target means to end an effect on that target that is ended at the end of their turn or ended by a saving throw.
